videos.script: Lesson 36 gave you finally, and with it a way to close a file however a method ends. This lesson starts by showing what that costs. {{leak}} First, a resource that is opened, used, and never closed, because the use threw. {{finally}} Then the repair with finally. It works, and it takes four lines and a variable outside the block. {{masked}} And it has a hole. When closing fails too, the second exception replaces the first, and the stack trace points at the wrong problem. {{twr}} Then the form of try that Java 7 added. You name the resource in parentheses, and the compiler writes the closing for you. Two resources close in the reverse of the order they opened. {{suppressed}} Last, where the lost exception goes. It is kept, attached to the first one, and printed under the word Suppressed. By the end, closing is something the compiler writes for you.
